clue.text: Greek writer a model brought over

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something brought over is turned across to the other side, so the word for model is read the other way round

parts.note: to model is to pose, as for an artist

explanation.surface: A Greek author is ferried across the sea with a fashion model in tow.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the model is turned round; the A stays in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop was the ancient Greek storyteller credited with the famous animal fables.

clue.text: Facing a junction

parts.note: taken as written
a cross is a crossroads, where roads meet

explanation.surface: Something is opposite a road junction.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'a junction' as A plus CROSS, a crossroads.
explanation.definitionFit: A house across the road is facing you, so the two words share the sense of being opposite.

clue.text: Finch is penetrating outer layer

indicators.note: a thing penetrating something has pushed its way inside it, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: skin is the outer layer of a body or fruit
taken as written

explanation.surface: A finch's beak is piercing something's outer coat.
explanation.definitionFit: The siskin is a small green and yellow songbird belonging to the finch family.

clue.text: Told cast

definitions.meaning: first meaning: informed someone of the facts
second meaning: given a part in a film, literally placed in the motion picture

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is literal: an actor who is cast has been put into a film.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means brought someone up to date with information, and read literally it describes casting an actor in a film.

clue.text: Sign of growth on island

indicators.note: in an across clue one thing placed on another follows it, so the growth comes after the island

parts.note: Capri is an island in the Bay of Naples
a corn is a hard growth of skin on the foot

explanation.surface: A foot complaint picked up while holidaying on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Growth' suggests crops, and corn does fit that reading too, but here it is the painful bump on a toe.
explanation.definitionFit: Capricorn, the goat, is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Narrow escape? One may be disputed in court

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a near miss, something that almost went wrong

definitions.text: One may be disputed in court
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a tight line decision by an umpire on a tennis court that a player may challenge

explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' suggests a law court, but it is a tennis court, where a line call too tight to judge easily is often contested.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a near miss, and in tennis a call on a ball landing near the line is literally a tight decision.

clue.text: Finished a dish

parts.note: something past is over and done with
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone has polished off a plate of food.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasta is an Italian staple food, served as a meal in many shapes such as spaghetti or penne.

clue.text: Saying last rites — talk so agonizingly

indicators.note: something done in agony is contorted and twisted, so the preceding letters are wrenched into a new order

parts.note: the fifteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A dying person's final sacrament is spoken with painful difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a proverb, a saying that the world contains every kind of person.

clue.text: First said about one with spirit

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the spoken word wraps round the rest

parts.note: oral means spoken rather than written
the Roman numeral for one
gin is a spirit; 'with' just joins it to the one

explanation.surface: Someone first spoke about a single person who had real spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' reads as courage, but here it is a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The original is the earliest version from which copies are made, so it came first.

clue.text: Head of organisation shot in dilapidated arena to which access is very restricted?

definitions.text: to which access is very restricted
definitions.note: describes the place rather than naming it: an area to which access is very restricted

indicators.note: in places the opening letter and the attempt inside the jumbled letters
a dilapidated building has fallen apart, so the letters of the venue are jumbled

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

indicators.note: the head of something is its top, so only the opening letter of the following word is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the word
a shot is an attempt, as in 'have a go'

explanation.surface: A company boss is gunned down in a run-down stadium that few may enter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' looks like gunfire but means an attempt. The jumbled arena splits after its first letter to take in the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-go area is a district that people are barred from or too afraid to enter.

clue.text: Dish is exaggerated in half of Rome

indicators.note: in places the first two words inside the part of the city name
half of a word keeps just one of its two halves, here the front portion of the city's name

parts.note: the first half of the city's name
taken as written
OTT is short for over the top

explanation.surface: A meal in Rome is served with excessive fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: OTT, for 'over the top', is common British slang for exaggerated.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is an Italian rice dish cooked slowly in stock.

clue.text: Badger's burrow in good location

parts.note: a sett is a badger's den
taken as written
G is the standard abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A badger has dug its home in a nice spot.
explanation.definitionFit: The setting of a story or building is its place or surroundings.

clue.text: Pick a screen that's free in research centre

indicators.note: letters set free are no longer held in place and can fall into any order

parts.note: the eleven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Choose any display monitor you like at the laboratory, as it costs nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A science park is a cluster of research and technology businesses, often linked to a university.

clue.text: Gershwin, inspirational in some degree

definitions.note: a surname standing for a first name

indicators.note: in some degree means partly, so only part of the next word is used

parts.note: found inside the word, letters four to six

explanation.surface: One of the Gershwins was something of an inspiration.
explanation.definitionFit: Ira Gershwin was the lyricist brother of composer George Gershwin.

clue.text: Perhaps monarch had foe tortured, say

indicators.note: a tortured body is twisted out of shape, so the letters before it are contorted

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
to state is to say

explanation.surface: A king or queen is said to have had an enemy tortured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks a monarch as one example; a president is another.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch is one kind of head of state, the formal leader of a country.

clue.text: Finished on path in high gear

indicators.note: in a down clue one thing on another sits above it, so the word for finished comes first

parts.note: a match that is over has finished
a drive is a private road or path up to a house

explanation.surface: Someone finished their run along the track at top speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Overdrive is an extra top gear in a car, so it is literally a high gear.

clue.text: Answer: draw off small measure if necessary

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for answer
to tap a barrel or tree is to draw liquid off it
an inch is a small unit of length

explanation.surface: A reply: pour off a tiny amount if you have to.
explanation.definitionFit: At a pinch is an idiom for if pressed or in an emergency, when nothing better is available.

clue.text: Bullfighter ripped a piece up

parts.note: tore is the past tense of tear, to rip
taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue up means reading from bottom to top, so the word for a gun runs backwards

parts.note: piece and rod are both American slang for a handgun

explanation.surface: A matador tore a scrap of something upward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece' suggests a fragment, but it is gangster slang for a gun, as is rod.
explanation.definitionFit: A toreador is a bullfighter, especially one on horseback.

clue.text: Painting, inaccurate portrayal of Molière plot

indicators.note: an inaccurate portrayal gets things wrong, so the letters that follow are put in a different order

parts.note: the eleven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A picture that misrepresents the storyline of a Molière comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also hints at the meaning, since this kind of painting is a deliberately deceptive portrayal.
explanation.definitionFit: Trompe l'oeil, French for deceive the eye, is a style of painting so realistic it looks three-dimensional.

clue.text: Steer straight

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a verb, to guide or show the way
second meaning: an adjective, going without a detour or frank

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like an instruction to drive straight on; the two words are a verb and an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: To direct is to guide someone's course, and a direct route or answer is a straight one.

clue.text: Son breaks rule causing one to quit

indicators.note: something that breaks into a thing gets inside it, so one letter goes into the other word

parts.note: a monarch's reign is their rule
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A son defies a regulation and is forced to leave his job.
explanation.definitionFit: To resign is to give up one's post, which is to quit it.

clue.text: Parking? That is an easy thing

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: Someone finds parking a doddle.
explanation.walkthrough: The sense comes from 'easy as pie'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pie stands for something simple in the idiom easy as pie, and is used alone for a cinch.

clue.text: Secret society needs it disguised

parts.note: a clan is a close-knit group or society

indicators.note: a disguised thing has its appearance changed, so the letters before it are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A secret society must keep its business under wraps.
explanation.definitionFit: Clandestine means done in secret, kept hidden from others.

clue.text: Letter Italian penned by a church

indicators.note: something penned is enclosed as in a pen, so the nationality sits inside the other pieces

parts.note: taken as written
CH is the abbreviation for church
IT is the abbreviation for Italian, as in gin and it

explanation.surface: A letter written by an Italian in a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penned' suggests writing, but it means enclosed.
explanation.definitionFit: Aitch is the spelt-out name of the letter H.

clue.text: Certainly agree bout must be fixed

parts.note: a nod shows agreement

indicators.note: something fixed has been tampered with or rigged, so the letters of the fight are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Of course I agree the boxing match must be rigged.
explanation.definitionFit: No doubt is an adverbial phrase meaning surely or certainly.

clue.text: Is first to receive a priest, one from Haifa?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: first to the word means only its opening letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of the word
taken as written
Eli is the priest in the Bible who raised Samuel

explanation.surface: Is someone first in line to welcome a priest from Haifa?
explanation.walkthrough: 'First to receive' looks like it means welcoming, but it just picks the first letter of receive.
explanation.definitionFit: Haifa is a port city in Israel, so a native of it is an Israeli; the question mark shows this is an example.

clue.text: Good luck symbol in cavalry — one reduces friction

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the U-shaped charm hung over doors for luck
second meaning: the iron plate nailed to a hoof to stop it wearing away on the ground

explanation.walkthrough: 'In cavalry' sets the scene for the second half, a cryptic description: on a cavalry mount, this is what protects each hoof from rubbing away on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A horseshoe is a lucky charm and also the metal plate fitted to a horse's hoof against wear.

clue.text: Silky material modelled at home

parts.note: a model sits, or sat, for an artist
someone who is in is at home

explanation.surface: A model posed at home in a silky outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Modelled' suggests fashion, but here it means posing for a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Satin is a smooth glossy fabric with a lustrous surface, traditionally woven from silk.
